subject: Re: Kickoff: DEN for small-data tabular classification
body:
Anders,

Plan.

Staffing: Farah 50% on reproduction and benchmarking -- the released simulation entry point gives us a clean start -- and Umar 40% on the science, especially the synthetic binary-task generation approach the paper uses to facilitate pre-training, which we will want to extend with task distributions closer to our customers' data.

Second workstream: even if DEN wins on accuracy, the pre-trained stack is too heavy for the per-customer serving path as-is. We are scoping and staffing a distillation training recipe built from scratch: Umar Costa leads the design at 50% with Vera Egede at 30% building the training pipeline. Target: a student that keeps the fixed embedding+classification behavior within 1 point of the teacher at a quarter of the serving footprint.

Compute: modest -- tabular-scale models, a handful of Titan A100s.

Reproduction by April 17 looks comfortable.

Daniela
